jobs.description:
Company Overview

Madison Taylor Design is a leading multidisciplinary design firm providing architectural, landscape architecture, interior design, furniture & decorating, project management, and construction services for clients in the residential, commercial, and hospitality sectors. Our mission is to deliver high-end design solutions that blend inspiration from nature with modern and sustainable materials.

At the heart of Madison Taylor Design is our people and the experience we create together. Our core values are the backbone of how we work, lead, collaborate, and make decisions — we believe exceptional work comes from exceptional teams, built on strong culture, clear expectations, trust, and accountability. We run on the Entrepreneurial Operating System (EOS®) to create clarity, accountability, and alignment as we scale.

Summary

We are seeking an experienced Head of Business Services to lead the finance and people functions at Madison Taylor Design. You will oversee our financial operations, including month-end close, financial reporting, cash flow, forecasting, banking relationships, and financial controls, while also leading human resources administration with the support of our outsourced HR partner.

As a member of our leadership team, reporting to the Integrator, you will build and lead our newly hired full-charge bookkeeper and administrative team, providing the financial insight, processes, and accountability needed to support the business. This is a hands-on leadership role requiring strong technical expertise, sound judgment, and the ability to work both strategically and in the details.
Reports to: Integrator

Location: Midhurst, ON — on-site

Employment Type: Full-time, permanent

Compensation: $95,000–$115,000 annually, commensurate with experience, plus quarterly performance bonus and profit share

Application Deadline: Hiring now — applications reviewed on a rolling basis

Key Responsibilities

Finance

Oversee the monthly financial close, reconciliations, and financial statements, ensuring accurate and timely reporting.
Develop and maintain annual budgets, rolling forecasts, cash-flow projections, and divisional profit and loss reporting for design, construction, and furniture.
Oversee project and construction job costing, client deposits and retainers, monthly billing, and financial reconciliations.
Manage banking relationships, including lender reporting, covenants, and credit facilities.
Oversee payroll, HST, source deductions, and year-end reporting in coordination with external accountants.
Establish and maintain financial controls, approval processes, and accounting procedures.
Provide hands-on technical accounting support, resolve complex issues, and identify opportunities to improve financial processes and reporting.

People & Human Resources

Serve as the primary point of contact for employee questions and concerns, handling matters fairly, promptly, and confidentially.
Oversee HR administration, including onboarding, employment agreements, employee records, benefits, and compliance with Ontario employment legislation.
Coordinate recruitment and the company-wide performance review process in partnership with department heads.
Support employee relations, performance management, and workplace matters, engaging the Integrator or outsourced HR advisor as appropriate.
Work with our outsourced HR partner to maintain employment contracts, company policies, procedures, and the employee handbook.

Leadership & Operations

Build, lead, mentor, and develop our newly hired full-charge bookkeeper and administrative team, establishing clear expectations and accountability.
Manage the company's insurance program and employee benefits plan, including renewals, coverage, and claims.
Oversee finance and HR systems, software accounts, and related vendor relationships, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency through technology, automation, and AI.
Collaborate with department leaders to support financial planning, reporting, and continuous improvement.
Participate actively in the leadership team, maintaining Scorecards and Rocks and contributing to weekly Level 10 Meetings through EOS®.

What You Bring

CPA designation, advanced progress toward a CPA designation, or equivalent accounting education and experience.
7+ years of progressive accounting experience
, including experience in a Controller, Finance Manager, or comparable financial leadership role (required).
Construction or project-based accounting experience
, ideally 3+ years, including project costing, reconciliations, and financial reporting (strongly preferred).
2+ years of human resources experience
, or experience managing HR responsibilities within a finance or business leadership role (preferred).
Advanced, hands-on QuickBooks Online and Excel skills, including complex reconciliations, financial reporting, and troubleshooting.
Strong experience with budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow management, and banking relationships.
Demonstrated ability to independently resolve complex accounting and HR matters, with sound judgment and attention to detail.
Experience leading and developing a small team, with the ability to delegate effectively while maintaining accountability.
Strong systems and process improvement skills, including experience implementing technology, automation, and operational efficiencies.
Experience in architecture, design, construction, or another project-based professional services environment is an asset.
Experience with EOS® is a significant asset.
Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with a high level of discretion and professionalism.

Why Join Us?

Lead the finance and people functions of a growing, 35-person multidisciplinary design and build firm.
Be part of a collaborative leadership team with meaningful responsibility and decision-making authority.
Help strengthen the systems, processes, and financial reporting that support our continued growth.
Work alongside talented designers, architects, and builders creating high-end homes across Ontario cottage country.
Competitive base salary, quarterly performance bonus, profit share, and benefits.

To Apply

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter, including an example of a finance or HR process you developed or improved and the impact it had on the organization.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Madison Taylor Design uses artificial intelligence to assist in screening, assessing, and selecting applicants as part of our recruitment process. Final hiring decisions are made by our team.

Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.

Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.

At Giant Tiger, our mission is simple: help Canadians save more every day. We’re a Canadian institution rooted in our communities and built on 60+ years of success. As part of our store support team, your work directly impacts stores across the country and drives the value that our customers see on the shelves.

We’re looking for people who are passionate about retail and motivated by meaningful work that makes a real impact. This posting represents a current opportunity at Giant Tiger.

Job Title

Head of Merchandise Operations & Financial Planning

About This Role

Giant Tiger is looking for a strategic merchandise leader to help shape the next chapter of our business as we strengthen our position as a Hard Discount retailer.

This is a significant merchandising leadership role with the opportunity to influence how Giant Tiger plans, operates and delivers value to Canadians. Reporting into our Executive Vice President and Chief Merchant, you will lead Merchandise Operations and Financial Planning, establishing the financial plans, operating rhythms and decision-making frameworks that guide our merchandising business. From sales, margin and inventory planning to pricing, promotions and space productivity, you will help ensure our merchandising strategies translate into disciplined execution, profitable growth and consistently low prices our customers can trust.

Giant Tiger operates differently than Canada's largest retailers. We are a Canadian-owned retailer with more than 260 stores, including a significant franchise network. Our success depends on keeping things simple, making disciplined decisions and ensuring our strategies can be executed consistently across our stores.

Workplace Arrangements

This role will follow a hybrid remote/onsite schedule. Applicants for this role can expect to work on-site from our Ottawa, Ontario Head Office throughout the month.

What You'll Be Doing

Develop Giant Tiger’s three-year rolling merchandise financial plan and annual fiscal plan to align sales, gross margin, inventory, pricing and other merchandise KPIs with approved strategic and financial priorities.
Design and continuously improve the ongoing merchandise operating model to establish effective planning processes, business-review rhythms, operating standards, decision mechanisms and recurring workflows.
Design and optimize the integrated merchandise planning framework, processes and operating rhythms that align MFP, Business Managers, Merchants and cross-functional partners in the development and execution of annual, seasonal and in-period plans.
Develop merchandise pricing and promotion strategy, policies and governance to strengthen low-price perception, support Hard Discount principles and deliver financial commitments.
Design visual merchandising direction, standards and governance to enable consistent, practical, and efficient execution of the merchandise vision across stores.
Establish and optimize enterprise merchandise space-planning principles, standards and decision frameworks to align selling-space allocation with customer demand, category strategy, enterprise priorities and financial productivity.

University Undergraduate degree in Business, Merchandising, or related field, and 10 years experience in the Retail Industry OR 15 years experience in the retail industry

Extensive knowledge of retail Merchandise Financial Planning process and metrics

Strong analytical skills with the ability to see future opportunities, challenge the status quo, make recommendations and problem solve
Strong ability to communicate effectively, interact and build relationships across all levels of the organization and with key partners
Strong ability to present information in an effective and concise manner to diverse audience and forums
Strong management skills (coaching, development and training skills) that build effective teams through the organization for succession
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and strong knowledge of Microsoft Office suite of products

Experience working in a large, multi-site national retailer

Position:

Director of FP&A

Company:

Solen Software Group

Location:

Full-time

About Solen Software Group

Solen Software Group is an evergreen holding company that acquires and operates proven software businesses that have significant growth potential in a variety of vertical markets, enabling them to be market leaders in their niche industry. Solen owns several software companies in various market spaces: Human Resource Technology, Fleet Telematics, Asset Management, E-Health, Document Management, and other innovative software solutions in a variety of industries. Solen is backed by a group of advisors and investors that have built software businesses of material scale (10-100M in ARR) and advised many.

About The Role

The Director of FP&A will own how Solen plans, forecasts, measures, and makes decisions across our portfolio of 20+ software companies and the holding company. Reporting to the CFO, this role partners as a peer with the Controller: the Controller owns the close, books, and consolidated actuals, while the Director of FP&A owns the budget, forecast, KPIs, Monthly Business Review, and the models behind capital allocation and acquisitions.

This is a build-as-you-go role. Our businesses run with real autonomy and span recurring SaaS, usage-based fees, professional services, and hardware. You will design the planning and reporting engine that replaces today's manual, company-by-company reporting, build the team that runs it, and support the CFO in raising debt and equity capital.

This is a highly strategic, hands-on leadership role working directly with the CFO, CEO, Portfolio Leaders, and General Managers of our operating companies (OpCos).

Key Responsibilities

Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting

Own the annual budget, quarterly re-forecast, rolling forecast, and long-range plan across all OpCos and the HoldCo, with one planning calendar and standard templates.
Build driver-based models suited to each revenue model: ARR, retention and churn cohorts, usage volumes, utilization and billable hours, hardware and license sales, and headcount.
Produce a consolidated, scenario-ready outlook for the CFO, CEO, and board.
Own forward cash forecasting and liquidity and covenant-headroom modelling in partnership with the Controller.
Track forecast accuracy, explain material misses, and continuously improve the process.

Portfolio Performance & KPIs

Define and deploy a consistent KPI framework across the portfolio, benchmarked against Solen's investment thesis.
Track unit economics, retention cohorts, customer profitability, and cost structure by function to benchmark OpCos against each other and best-in-class.
Support OpCo leaders on pricing, customer profitability, cost optimization, and financial turnarounds.

Monthly Business Review & Reporting

Own the MBR cadence, structure, KPI package, and follow-through on action items, raising the quality of insight in every review.
Partner with divisional controllers who run OpCo-level MBRs, equipping them with better data, tools, and insight.
Standardize and automate management reporting and dashboards in Power BI, and develop digital, real-time, and AI-native reporting.
Own the reporting roadmap, defining every metric once and building core reports such as the ARR bridge, budget-versus-actual, organic versus inorganic growth, EBITDA bridge, free cash flow, 13-week cash forecast, and return on invested capital.

Capital Allocation, Capital Raising & M&A

Build the models that guide capital allocation across reinvestment, bolt-on acquisitions, and cash returned to the HoldCo.
Support the CFO and deal team with acquisition models: valuation, diligence, pro formas, and synergy cases.
Support the CFO on debt and equity raises and refinancing with models, projections, scenario analysis, and lender and investor materials.
Track post-acquisition performance against the underwriting case and onboard new acquisitions into planning and KPIs from day one.

FP&A Team Build-Out

Design the FP&A operating model for a lean, decentralized portfolio.
Recruit, hire, and develop a best-in-class FP&A and business partner team.
Establish clear ownership between FP&A, the Controller, divisional controllers, and OpCo finance leaders.
Foster a culture of ownership, candor, and continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, accounting, or a related field; MBA or CFA preferred.
8+ years of progressive FP&A, corporate finance, or strategic finance experience.
Direct ownership of budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning for a multi-entity or decentralized business (e.g., PE-backed platform, roll-up, or multi-brand company).
Experience building, leading, and developing an FP&A or business partner team.
Excellent financial modelling skills, including driver-based forecasting and scenario analysis; advanced Excel.
Experience designing KPI frameworks and running recurring business reviews with operating leaders.
Experience building management reporting and dashboards in a BI tool.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to turn complex analysis into clear recommendations for a CEO, board, or non-finance operator.
Willing to work on-site in Salt Lake City or Park City, UT, or in New York, NY with regular travel to Utah, and occasional international travel to Lisbon, Portugal.
Legally authorized to work in the United States.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in B2B or vertical market SaaS, including ARR, GRR/NRR, and cohort analysis.
Experience modelling mixed revenue streams: subscription, usage-based, professional services, and hardware.
Background in private equity, permanent capital, investment banking, or Big-4 transaction advisory.
Experience supporting debt or equity raises or refinancing.
Experience using AI tools to automate manual finance work.
Working knowledge of Power BI and Sage Intacct or a comparable multi-entity ERP.
Experience with multi-currency planning and teams based outside the U.S.

Not every candidate will meet every requirement. If you have shown real trajectory and results, we encourage you to apply.

What Success Looks Like

One planning and forecasting engine is live across all OpCos and the HoldCo, with a full budget cycle and rolling forecast completed and forecast accuracy improving.
A consistent KPI framework is adopted by every OpCo, with each company viewed on one comparable scorecard against Solen's investment thesis.
The MBR runs on a predictable cadence with a standardized, automated package, and the highest-priority reports are live.
The FP&A function is defined, first hires are ramping, and manual reporting has come off the accounting team.
Capital allocation, acquisition, and financing models exist and have informed real decisions.
The CFO, CEO, Portfolio Leaders, and GMs seek FP&A's view before major decisions.

Solen-isms (How We Operate)

Ownership Mindset: We own the mission. We don't wait to be told. We lead, fix, and build as if it were ours. When problems arise, we run toward them, not away.
Benchmark to Best: We seek out excellence. We measure ourselves against the best and adapt quickly, always looking for the edge that moves us forward.
Openly Self-Critical: Leaders go first: they surface their misses early, ask for direct feedback, and turn “game film” into better decisions and better systems.
Disagree & Commit: Leaders disagree openly and constructively, regardless of title or tenure, because truth is how we avoid bureaucracy and benchmark to best.
Figureitoutiveness: Embracing challenges, fostering growth, and taking initiative, leaders thrive on hard work and high failure tolerance.
Mutual Elevation: Committed to growth, elevating teams, developing future leaders, and removing barriers to mastery and joy.
Learn-it-alls: Learn-it-alls, not know-it-alls, embracing failure as part of growth and progress.
Pioneering: Pioneering driven by opportunity, using first principles thinking and unbound by tradition or rules.
Will to Win: Leaders relentlessly pursue potential, reject mediocrity, and get what they tolerate.
Dialectical: We learn through conversation. We ask, listen, question, and evolve — valuing disagreement as a tool for alignment and deeper understanding.
Frugality: Achieving more with less, focusing on quality, long-term value, and company-wide responsibility.
Candor: We communicate with integrity, transparency, and respect in all conversations.
Kaizen: Kaizen is continuous improvement as a way of life. Leaders make hundreds of small upgrades that compound, turning lessons into standards and standards into durable systems.

Recruitment Disclaimer

Solen Software Group will never request payment, banking information, or other sensitive personal or financial details during any stage of the recruitment process. All official communication will come from a verified @solensoftwaregroup.com email address. Any outreach outside these standards should be disregarded and reported through our official channels.

À propos du Centre Mechtilde

Depuis 45 ans, le Centre Mechtilde accompagne et soutient les femmes et leurs enfants vivant des situations de violence conjugale, familiale ou toute autre forme de violence. Au fil des années, l'organisme a su faire évoluer ses services pour répondre aux besoins changeants des femmes et aux réalités de la société, dans une approche inclusive, accueillante et respectueuse de la diversité.

Le Centre Mechtilde offre notamment un service d’hébergement d’une capacité de 17 places, accessible 24 heures sur 24, 7 jours sur 7, ainsi que des services d'accompagnement visant à favoriser la sécurité, l'autonomie et le mieux-être des femmes et de leurs enfants. Depuis 2018, l'organisme assure également la gestion de La Maison Marie Jacque, un projet de logement communautaire comptant 31 logements, destiné aux femmes et à leurs enfants confrontés à des enjeux de stabilité résidentielle ou à un risque d'itinérance.

Pour réaliser sa mission, le Centre peut compter sur une équipe de 28 employées, réparties entre l'administration (3 personnes, incluant la direction générale), la coordination (2 personnes) et l'intervention (23 employées syndiquées). Ensemble, elles contribuent à offrir un milieu sécurisant et des services favorisant le développement de l'autonomie, la création de relations saines et l'atteinte des objectifs personnels des femmes accompagnées.

Rôle de la directrice générale

La directrice générale exerce un leadership mobilisateur, humain et stratégique, guidé par les valeurs et la mission du Centre Mechtilde et de La Maison Marie Jacque. Elle joue un rôle clé dans la consolidation, le développement et le rayonnement de l'organisme, tout en veillant à offrir un environnement sécurisant et bienveillant aux femmes et à leurs enfants. En étroite collaboration avec le conseil d'administration, les équipes et les partenaires du milieu, elle assure la pérennité de l'organisation, favorise la mobilisation des ressources et contribue à l'évolution des services en réponse aux besoins des femmes accompagnées.

Sommaire des fonctions

Sous l'autorité du conseil d'administration, la directrice générale assure la gestion globale des activités et des ressources humaines, financières, matérielles et administratives du Centre Mechtilde et de La Maison Marie Jacque. Elle veille à la qualité et à la continuité des services, encadre les équipes de gestion et assure le respect des politiques, des obligations organisationnelles et de la convention collective. Elle travaille étroitement avec le conseil d'administration à la mise en œuvre des orientations stratégiques, à la saine gouvernance et à l'atteinte des objectifs de l'organisme. Elle assure également le développement des partenariats et la représentation de l'organisme auprès des acteurs du milieu.

Tâches et responsabilités

Gestion stratégique et opérationnelle

Participer à l'élaboration des orientations stratégiques et assurer la mise en œuvre des plans d'action qui en découlent.
Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les deux coordonnatrices afin d'assurer la qualité, la cohérence et la continuité des services.
Superviser le bon fonctionnement des deux installations et veiller à une utilisation optimale des ressources matérielles.

Gestion des ressources humaines

Assurer une gestion efficace des ressources humaines de l’organisation.

Favoriser un climat de travail sain, collaboratif et respectueux des valeurs de l'organisme.
Assurer une gestion harmonieuse des relations de travail dans un environnement syndiqué, conformément à la convention collective en vigueur.

Gestion financière et administrative

Représenter l’organisation lors d'événements, de rencontres de concertation et d'activités officielles de l'organisme dans son milieu.
Identifier les occasions de collaboration et de développement favorisant la réalisation de la mission.
Agir à titre de porte-parole de l'organisme, selon les orientations établies avec le conseil d'administration.

Profil recherché

Diplôme universitaire de 1er cycle dans un domaine relié à l’administration, en sciences sociales (psychologie, travail social, relations industrielles), en psychoéducation ou dans un domaine connexe.
Expérience de 3 à 5 ans dans un poste de gestion similaire incluant la supervision d’employées (en milieu syndiqué, un atout) et la gestion du budget.

À propos du Centre Mechtilde

Depuis 45 ans, le Centre Mechtilde accompagne et soutient les femmes et leurs enfants vivant des situations de violence conjugale, familiale ou toute autre forme de violence. Au fil des années, l'organisme a su faire évoluer ses services pour répondre aux besoins changeants des femmes et aux réalités de la société, dans une approche inclusive, accueillante et respectueuse de la diversité.

Le Centre Mechtilde offre notamment un service d’hébergement d’une capacité de 17 places, accessible 24 heures sur 24, 7 jours sur 7, ainsi que des services d'accompagnement visant à favoriser la sécurité, l'autonomie et le mieux-être des femmes et de leurs enfants. Depuis 2018, l'organisme assure également la gestion de La Maison Marie Jacque, un projet de logement communautaire comptant 31 logements, destiné aux femmes et à leurs enfants confrontés à des enjeux de stabilité résidentielle ou à un risque d'itinérance.

Pour réaliser sa mission, le Centre peut compter sur une équipe de 28 employées, réparties entre l'administration (3 personnes, incluant la direction générale), la coordination (2 personnes) et l'intervention (23 employées syndiquées). Ensemble, elles contribuent à offrir un milieu sécurisant et des services favorisant le développement de l'autonomie, la création de relations saines et l'atteinte des objectifs personnels des femmes accompagnées.

Rôle de la directrice générale

La directrice générale exerce un leadership mobilisateur, humain et stratégique, guidé par les valeurs et la mission du Centre Mechtilde et de La Maison Marie Jacque. Elle joue un rôle clé dans la consolidation, le développement et le rayonnement de l'organisme, tout en veillant à offrir un environnement sécurisant et bienveillant aux femmes et à leurs enfants. En étroite collaboration avec le conseil d'administration, les équipes et les partenaires du milieu, elle assure la pérennité de l'organisation, favorise la mobilisation des ressources et contribue à l'évolution des services en réponse aux besoins des femmes accompagnées.

Sommaire des fonctions

Sous l'autorité du conseil d'administration, la directrice générale assure la gestion globale des activités et des ressources humaines, financières, matérielles et administratives du Centre Mechtilde et de La Maison Marie Jacque. Elle veille à la qualité et à la continuité des services, encadre les équipes de gestion et assure le respect des politiques, des obligations organisationnelles et de la convention collective. Elle travaille étroitement avec le conseil d'administration à la mise en œuvre des orientations stratégiques, à la saine gouvernance et à l'atteinte des objectifs de l'organisme. Elle assure également le développement des partenariats et la représentation de l'organisme auprès des acteurs du milieu.

Tâches et responsabilités

Gestion stratégique et opérationnelle
Assurer la gestion globale des activités et des services.
Veiller à l'application des politiques, des procédures et des orientations organisationnelles.
Participer à l'élaboration des orientations stratégiques et assurer la mise en œuvre des plans d'action qui en découlent.
Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les deux coordonnatrices afin d'assurer la qualité, la cohérence et la continuité des services.
Superviser le bon fonctionnement des deux installations et veiller à une utilisation optimale des ressources matérielles.

Gestion des ressources humaines
Superviser, soutenir et mobiliser les membres de l'équipe sous sa responsabilité directe.
Assurer une gestion efficace des ressources humaines de l’organisation.
Veiller à l'application des politiques et des pratiques de gestion des ressources humaines ainsi qu'au respect des obligations de l'employeur.
Favoriser un climat de travail sain, collaboratif et respectueux des valeurs de l'organisme.
Assurer une gestion harmonieuse des relations de travail dans un environnement syndiqué, conformément à la convention collective en vigueur.

Gestion financière et administrative
Assurer une saine gestion financière de l'organisme et veiller à sa pérennité.
Superviser l'élaboration des budgets annuels et assurer le suivi des résultats financiers.
Veiller au respect des exigences des bailleurs de fonds et des obligations de reddition de comptes.
Assurer le suivi des ressources financières et matérielles en fonction des priorités organisationnelles.
Contribuer à la recherche et au maintien des sources de financement nécessaires à la réalisation de la mission.

Gouvernance et collaboration avec le conseil d'administration
Collaborer étroitement avec le conseil d'administration et sa présidence dans la réalisation des orientations et des priorités de l'organisme.
Préparer les rencontres du conseil d'administration, documenter les dossiers et transmettre les informations nécessaires à la prise de décision.
Assurer le suivi et la mise en œuvre des décisions du conseil d'administration.

Relations avec le milieu, partenariats et représentation
Développer et entretenir des relations de collaboration avec les partenaires communautaires, institutionnels et financiers.
Représenter l’organisation lors d'événements, de rencontres de concertation et d'activités officielles de l'organisme dans son milieu.
Identifier les occasions de collaboration et de développement favorisant la réalisation de la mission.
Agir à titre de porte-parole de l'organisme, selon les orientations établies avec le conseil d'administration.

Profil recherché

Diplôme universitaire de 1er cycle dans un domaine relié à l’administration, en sciences sociales (psychologie, travail social, relations industrielles), en psychoéducation ou dans un domaine connexe.
Expérience de 3 à 5 ans dans un poste de gestion similaire incluant la supervision d’employées (en milieu syndiqué, un atout) et la gestion du budget.
Expérience en gestion de budgets d’OBNL avec une approche stricte, transparente et rigoureuse.
Expérience à travailler avec des maisons d’aide et d’hébergement pour femmes victimes de violence, un atout.
Expérience à diriger une équipe de professionnelles multidisciplinaires.
Expérience de collaboration avec un conseil d’administration.
Habileté marquée pour la reddition de comptes et la gestion rigoureuse de subventions.
Capacité à optimiser les ressources financières dans un contexte limité.
Leadership positif et collaboratif.
Éthique professionnelle, bon jugement, autonomie, sens de l’initiative, sens de l’organisation, capacité à prendre des décisions difficiles, bonne capacité d’adaptation et rigueur.
Bonne maîtrise du français à l’oral et à l’écrit, et bilinguisme considéré comme un atout.
Capacité à se déplacer de façon autonome entre deux sites de travail et disponibilité pour effectuer d’autres déplacements occasionnels.

Conditions de travail

Poste permanent à temps plein avec horaire flexible ayant une moyenne de 40 heures par semaine. Disponibilité requise occasionnellement en soirée et certaines fins de semaine, lors de la tenue d’événements et de rencontres.
